subject: Where requests land and delete guarantees — HelioHealth Q&A
messages:
From: Maya Rios <security@heliohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Lin <d.lin@cybermapped.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where LLM requests are executed + deletion guarantees

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Before we take the tech screen to procurement we need a short factual Q&A to satisfy HelioHealth's InfoSec team and our external vendor assessor (copied). Specifically: 

1) For Redwood's hosted API (the one you demoed) where are inference requests executed geographically? Please list regions/hypervisor locations and the subprocessors responsible for compute and object storage.

2) Can we contractually require all execution and persistent storage for our tenant to remain inside the US (no EU/APAC hops) for both live inference and batch embeddings? If so, what proof do you provide?

3) What is your default retention for request logs, prompt/response telemetry, and derived artifacts (embeddings, caches)? What is the deletion workflow and SLA from request to confirmed purge?

4) Are there any cross-border transfers (e.g., for backups, monitoring, CDN) we should be aware of, and which subprocessors might be involved?

Attached is our standard vendor questionnaire (short) — please fill the first two pages and return. We need a concise one-page attestation we can share with compliance.

Can you respond by EOD Thursday PST? If you prefer, schedule a short call.

Thanks,
Maya Rios
Head of Information Security
HelioHealth

——

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where LLM requests are executed + deletion guarantees

Maya — great questions, thank you. High level answers below; attaching a short execution map and a proposed attestation. Neha from our security & legal team is cc'd and will add specifics around subprocessors and contractual language.

1) Execution geography (hosted API):
- Our hosted API runs on cloud regions we operate in the US (primary: us-east-1, us-west-2) when a customer configures US-only routing.
- Subprocessors for compute: AWS (EC2/GPU fleets) and GCP in select cases for specialized hardware; object storage: AWS S3.
- For customers that do not opt into multi-region routing, we default to routing that favors the nearest available capacity; for HelioHealth we can pin routing to US-only.

2) US-only contractual restriction:
- Yes — for enterprise customers we offer a US-only processing commitment for hosted + Dedicated deployments. That includes: routing policy that pins requests to US regions, contract clause in the DPA, and configuration that avoids cross-region model falls back.
- Proof: we can provide an execution map (attached) plus per-request routing logs for a 14-day sample, and a signed attestation on company letterhead. For a stronger guarantee we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) which provide capacity isolation and additional assurances.

3) Retention & deletion:
- Default telemetry retention (hosted): 30 days for request logs/telemetry, 90 days for aggregated performance metrics.
- Derived artifacts: embeddings and cached prefixes are retained only if customer enables persistence; default is not persisted beyond ephemeral caches; if enabled, embeddings are retained per contract (typical enterprise choice: 30/90/365 days).
- Deletion workflow: deletion requests are submitted via console/API -> queued and executed by the orchestration layer -> background erase job removes objects and invalidates caches -> audit entry created. SLA: 30 days for complete purge from persistent storage; for Dedicated/Private we can negotiate shorter windows and supply confirmation evidence.

4) Cross-border transfers:
- By default (global deployments) there may be cross-border hops for provisioning, model updates, and CDN delivery. For US-only commitments we disable cross-region routing and avoid non-US subprocessors for execution. 
- Monitoring/observability vendors (Datadog/Segment) may process metadata; we can contractually restrict which telemetry fields are exported and where.

Attached: redwood-us-exec-map-2026.pdf (illustrative execution map) and a one-page attestation draft. If that looks good we can produce the formal attestation and a 14-day routing sample for your assessor.

Next steps: I can (a) fill the questionnaire with Neha, (b) provide the signed attestation, and (c) set up a short technical call for Thursday. Which do you want first?

Best,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where LLM requests are executed + deletion guarantees

Maya / Jordan — adding more concrete subprocessors and contractual language you can rely on. I'm Neha (Security & Privacy).

Subprocessors (execution & storage) we may use for US-only customers:
- AWS (primary): EC2/GPU instances (us-east-1, us-west-2), S3 for object storage.
- GCP (us-west2): only used when specialized hardware requested and explicitly agreed in contract.
- Cloudflare: edge routing/CDN for API front door (can be configured to US-only PoPs in enterprise plan).
- HashiCorp Vault/KMS providers for key management integrations (customer-managed keys supported via KMS/HSM).
- Internal observability: Datadog (optional); we can disable automatic export of PII telemetry.

Contract language and controls: 
- DPA addendum: we will include a US-processing addendum that requires Redwood to (a) route execution to US regions only, (b) not export persistent customer content outside the US, and (c) notify HelioHealth prior to any change in subprocessors that would affect jurisdiction.
- Evidence: upon signature we will provide: (1) a 14‑day per-request routing sample (anonymized request IDs + region stamps), (2) an export of subprocessor roster, and (3) a signed attestation of execution locus. For higher assurance we can supply time-limited access to our audit logs or a security report (redwood-audit-evidence-pack.zip attached).

Retention / deletion nuance: 
- For hosted API you flagged, default 30-day telemetry retention is accurate. Important: certain ephemeral runtime caches (KV caches) can persist for session duration and are not written to persistent object storage unless the customer opts in.
- Deletion confirmation: background jobs may take up to 30 days to fully remove replicated artifacts from all layers; we will provide a deletion certificate once the purge completes. For Dedicated we can reduce the purge window to 7 days as a contractual SLA.

Cross-border exceptions:
- Backups: point-in-time backups for disaster recovery may be replicated depending on your chosen availability options — we will exclude non-US replication for HelioHealth if requested in contract.
- Support access: if you elect 24/7 global support involving non-US staff, we will require an explicit agreement; otherwise support access can be restricted to US-based personnel for this account.

Attachments included for your assessor: redwood-audit-evidence-pack.zip (contains sample routing logs, subprocessors.csv, and an attestation template).

If you want, Marissa can run a technical deep-dive on Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs tomorrow. Proposed MAT (mutual action plan) in the Drive link.

-Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
